name: Sathyamurthi Perumal Temple, Thirumayam
deity: Vishnu as Sathyamurthi Perumal (Sathyagiri Nathan), with the Goddess Uyyavandha Nachiyar — and, in the rock-cut cave, reclining on the serpent Adisesha
period: A Divya Desam of the Pandya country, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
dynasty: Muttaraiyar cave sanctum, with later Pandya halls
style: Rock-cut cave sanctum with Dravidian mandapas
summary: Below the fort hill of Thirumayam, Vishnu reclines on Adisesha in a rock-cut cave beside his shrine as Sathyamurthi Perumal — a Divya Desam of the Pandya country sung by Thirumangai Alvar.

sections.history: Thirumayam, the Thiru-Meyyam or "sacred hill of truth" of the Alvars, rises in the Pudukkottai country, and its Vishnu shrine is cut into the southern face of the hill. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams, counted among the abodes of Pandya Nadu, and was sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. Scholars place the cave temple in the closing decades of the seventh century and associate it with the Muttaraiyar chiefs: an inscription records its renovation and an endowment by Perumbidugu Perundevi, mother of a Muttaraiyar vassal of the Pallava king Nandivarman II. Pillared halls were added before the cave, mostly in the later Pandya period, and the hill above carries the walls of Thirumayam Fort.
sections.architecture: The heart of the temple is a rock-cut cave on the south side of Satyagiri hill. Its great relief shows Vishnu reclining on the coiled serpent Adisesha, carved in the living rock and some fifteen feet long with the Goddess at his chest. Sathyamurthi Perumal is enshrined beneath a single-storeyed Dravidian vimana, and the Goddess Uyyavandha Nachiyar has her separate sannidhi. Later Pandya mandapas lead in to the cave. A Shiva cave of the Pandya period lies beside it on the same hill.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that the sage Satya performed penance at this hill, and that Vishnu, pleased, revealed himself here as the embodiment of truth — Sathyamurthi, Lord of Satyagiri. Tradition holds that for the sage the Lord turned the river into the temple tank, the rock into the sacred Meyyam hill and a banyan into the holy fig, so that the whole place became his abode. The name Thirumayam itself is remembered as a softening of Thiru-Meyyam, the hill of truth.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the great Vaishnava calendar — Vaikunta Ekadashi, the processions of Sathyamurthi Perumal and the Goddess on their festival vehicles, and the days of the Alvars, Thirumangai Alvar above all. Festival dates follow the Tamil calendar; confirm them locally.
sections.experience: A rare Divya Desam where the pilgrim stands before the living rock: the reclining Lord in the cave and Sathyamurthi Perumal in his shrine are worshipped within a few steps of each other. Many combine the visit with the Shiva cave beside it and a climb to the fort ramparts above.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi and festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirumayam lies on the Pudukkottai–Karaikudi road, about 20 km south of Pudukkottai, and has a railway station on the Tiruchirappalli–Karaikudi line; the nearest airport is Tiruchirappalli. The temple sits at the foot of the fort hill, a short walk from the town.
